races.name: Enter ITV7 For Free EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Sky Bet For The Fans Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Two B Tanned
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a win over this exact course, trip and going (1/8f/GOO) giving her solid course claims; fitted with hood and has run from the front throughout, but a 47-day absence and a T14 strike rate of just 1/19 for Camacho tempers confidence, and she must handle Quisana's challenge for the lead without blowing her chance.|
runners_data.comment: Two B Tanned won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a genuine threat at a competitive mark of 86; the main risk is a return from 47 days off, with her last two efforts both well below that winning level.

runners_data.name: Si Grass
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old is lightly exposed at this trip, having won over 8f on Standard ground, and Callum Shepherd gives her an experienced rider; only 1 from 4 on similar going is a modest record, and she must settle promptly behind the expected pace duel to make her prominent style pay here.|
runners_data.comment: Ran over today's trip and struck form three starts back, Si Grass arrives on the back of a second two starts back to suggest she retains ability; that disappointing eighth last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Luna Celeste
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's three-year-old arrives in excellent form — two wins from her last four runs including over 8f Good — and Tudhope's ability to time a run from a prominent position is a notable asset; strong sim-going record of 2W from 3 runs on comparable ground makes Good to Firm no concern, and she looks ideally profiled for this contested-pace scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Luna Celeste arrives in fine fettle after a win last time out, and her recent record of two wins in her last five starts underlines consistent form; she has run over today's distance and going before, and a low draw in stall two adds further appeal.

runners_data.name: Darzah
runners_data.note: William Haggas has a solid T14 rate of 7/43 and Cieren Fallon knows how to deliver a late challenge, but Darzah's recent form is inconsistent (5-1-8-1-5) and being the lone hold-up horse in a field of five risks getting too far back if the pace collapses; her one win over this trip and going (1/8f/GOO) shows the ability is there when conditions are right.|
runners_data.comment: Darzah won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, so the conditions pose no unknown, and her rating of 88 sees her share top billing here. The fifth last time out is the concern, though 26 days off may have freshened her up.

runners_data.name: Quisana
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old won last time out over 8f Good and has strong sim-going stats (1W3P from 5 runs on Good), but carrying the lowest weight (127lbs) and racing only 13 days after her last run needs monitoring; she must win the early battle for the lead against Two B Tanned or risk racing in an uncomfortable box, and her headgear flag (h) suggests she's already been managed for tractability.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of five on our figures and with a speed rating of 72, Quisana is hard to fancy despite winning last time out and returning fit on 13 days' rest; she has run over today's trip and going, but that counts for little when the ratings gap is this stark.

races.paceDynamic: Two B Tanned and Quisana are both confirmed front-runners, setting up a contested early pace over this flat Pontefract mile on Good to Firm ground, with neither likely to concede the lead without a fight. The duel between them will drive an honest, possibly pressured gallop from the outset, stretching the field and burning off reserves earlier than a solo-led race would. Si Grass and Luna Celeste will look to track close behind in prominent positions, while Darzah — the sole hold-up horse — is the one most likely to be handed a genuine pace to chase down. This contested lead scenario, with two horses doing each other's running, classically favours closers or horses racing just off the pace with a clean run, making the prominent-to-midfield profile of Luna Celeste and the late challenge of Darzah the styles best positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Two B Tanned and Quisana fight each other for the lead and set a genuine end-to-end gallop that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other out through the first half, leaving the race to be won from off the pace in the final two furlongs; horses who've tracked or come from behind arrive with energy to spare.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace horses (most likely Two B Tanned on higher OR and proven win from front) establishes a clear lead with Quisana unable to sustain the battle.
scenarios.body: A single horse controls tempo at a comfortable clip and rations its effort, arriving at the final furlong with enough left to hold on; the race becomes a test of willingness rather than a stamina grind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the front-runners tie each other up and Si Grass or Luna Celeste pounce early in the straight without needing to come wide.
scenarios.body: Sitting just behind the scrapping leaders, a prominent horse gets a dream run through with minimal effort expended; Good to Firm conditions keep the ground quick enough to reward that economical mid-race position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Arrives Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly fierce and unsustainable, leaving a clear path through for Darzah to pick off tiring rivals in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Darzah has won over this trip and going before (1/8f/GOO) and Cieren Fallon is adept at timing late challenges, but the sole hold-up role in a small field of five means traffic risk is real and the move must be perfectly timed.

watchPoints.text: Two B Tanned and Quisana — watch the first two furlongs closely; if both dig in hard for the lead, the resulting contested gallop could leave both emptied by the home turn, dramatically opening up the race for those behind.

Darzah — Cieren Fallon will need to find a gap in a small five-runner field; if the front-runners don't create enough pace, a hold-up horse can be left with nowhere to go and no cover to travel behind.

Si Grass — her 1/4 sim-going record is the thinnest in the field; if Good to Firm conditions prove faster than her previous Standard-ground wins suggest she handles, she may find the ground inconvenient at a key moment.
Luna Celeste — her trainer Tom Clover has hit 5 from 14 over the last 14 days, making her one of the yard's more live runners; monitor market moves before post time as stable confidence appears high.

Quisana's quick turnaround (13 days) is worth noting on Good to Firm — jockey Charles Bishop will need to judge the pace battle with Two B Tanned carefully or risk running a flat race on residual fatigue.

races.name: EBF Sky Bet Club Flying Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Arabian Dusk
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning after 382 days off, which is a significant fitness concern in a Listed race; Simon & Ed Crisford send her fresh and her sim-going figures show limited success on good, so she is on watch rather than trusted.
runners_data.comment: Arabian Dusk has run over today's trip and going, and with her trainer landing 33% of runners in the past fortnight she arrives with strong yard momentum — yet a 382-day absence and a winless recent sequence make fitness the obvious question mark.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Rose
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse stepping back from 7f-8f trips where she has struggled for form, and her record on good ground in this grade — zero wins and zero places from 15 similar-going runs — makes the case for her very hard to construct.
runners_data.comment: Brazilian Rose has won once in her last six starts, with unplaced her most recent effort 18 days ago, and she rates well below her official mark on our figures, ranking ninth of eleven; draw one and experience over today's trip and going are modest positives, but the overall profile makes her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Dash Of Azure
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up filly who has placed twice at this trip and goes on good ground; Ralph Beckett's 7/34 in 14 days suggests stable is in fair form, and her consistency at 7f on good suggests she will see out 6f strongly from the back.
runners_data.comment: Dash Of Azure has shown she can hit the frame, with a pair of runner-up finishes in her last five starts, yet she remains without a win and her most recent outing ended in an unplaced effort; she has run over today's trip and going before, returning fit on 18 days' rest, but 130 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Magic Basma
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's prominent filly has placed in two of her last three at 6f on good ground and handles this trip well; OR 102 gives her a class edge over several rivals and she should find a comfortable position just off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in her last five starts and carrying a rating of 102, Magic Basma has experience over today's trip and going, making her a genuine threat from stall 11; however, a 50-day absence and a trainer firing at just 3% lately are real concerns for a filly yet to win.

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's 3-year-old has a clean record on good ground (6 runs, all on similar going) and Daniel Tudhope is an astute pilot for prominent types; the drop from 7f to 6f is a minor query but her form profile suits this shape well.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in her last five starts, America Queen brings solid recent form into this, and having run over today's trip and going she arrives without an obvious excuse; yet to score in recent starts but shapes as the one to beat from stall two off 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Catching The Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who won twice earlier in the season but has posted back-to-back zeros since; the trainer Fahey yard has four winners from 29 in 14 days suggesting respectable form, and the drop in distance from her winning mark is small enough to overlook.
runners_data.comment: Catching The Moon has won twice in her last five starts, with back-to-back victories three and four starts back, though two unplaced runs since temper enthusiasm; she has run over today's trip and going, and 37 days off leaves fitness an open question from stall nine carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Killavia
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's 3-year-old has genuine front-running credentials — her last win was a 5f bolt-on — but with Miss Nightcap already owning the rail and a superior OR, she is almost certain to end up racing in a midfield position that does not flatter her; her STYLE_FIT of 0.94 reflects real positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom-two on our figures and rated 6 lb below her official mark, Killavia is hard to fancy in this company despite that recent win, though she has run over today's trip and going before and comes here on a reasonable 23-day break.

runners_data.name: Miss Nightcap
runners_data.note: The one true leader in the field; four runs, four positions at the sharp end, and a winning record over 6f-7f on good ground make her the pace anchor, and uncontested lead on good-to-firm should allow her to sustain fractions that will test those who follow.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Miss Nightcap faces a stiff ask off 127 lb, yet her recent form reads well — a winner last time out and two starts back, with distance and going experience in her favour.

runners_data.name: Royal Fixation
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's top-rated runner at OR 108 carries the class certificate and has two wins and four places from six runs on good ground at this trip; fitted with a tongue-strap and Sam James takes the ride — on raw ability she is the most credentialed here.
runners_data.comment: Royal Fixation arrives here with a win and a third in recent starts — strong evidence she belongs at this level — and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the worry is that her last two outings brought a seventh and a fifth, so she will need to recapture that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Ruby's Angel
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly is a natural front-runner whose most recent win came over this trip on good; however her OR of 84 is the lowest in the field and, placed in a midfield role by necessity rather than by nature, her chance depends on a positional gift she is unlikely to receive.
runners_data.comment: Ruby's Angel won five starts back and was second six starts back, but has not threatened since, finishing fourth twice and fifth last time out nineteen days ago; she has distance and going experience and a speed rating above her official mark, yet a trainer in poor recent form is a concern.

runners_data.name: Sing The Blues
runners_data.note: Three wins from five on good ground over 6f is a striking record and Cieren Fallon is an excellent handler of pace scenarios; her true style is prominent-to-lead, but in this field she will be shuffled back from her preferred slot, and winning from a compromised position asks more than her OR of 90 suggests she can give.
runners_data.comment: Sing The Blues has won three of her last five starts, including back-to-back victories, though a pulled-up effort three starts back gives pause; she has run over today's trip and going before, but 127 lb is a stiff ask and our rating leaves her ranked mid-division.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Nightcap is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press her for the lead, she should slot onto the front uncontested and set a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground at Pontefract. Royal Fixation, Magic Basma, and America Queen will push forward to dispute the prominent positions behind her, meaning the first two furlongs will be brisk but not chaotic, as these are all well-mannered prominent types rather than tearaway speedsters. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Sing The Blues, Killavia, and Ruby's Angel are all genuine prominent horses who are mapped to midfield because they are unlikely to claim their preferred position against stronger rivals in this grade. This race shape — an uncontested leader setting honest fractions with a wall of prominent horses behind — favours confirmed hold-up horses or those comfortable settling in midfield, as the strong pace set by Miss Nightcap and sustained by the prominent pack will serve those who conserve energy early and deliver late, with Dash Of Azure and Catching The Moon the clearest beneficiaries of that profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Miss Nightcap Controls, Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Nightcap leads uncontested and the prominent wall sets honest fractions, draining reserves from mid-race.
scenarios.body: Miss Nightcap ensures a true test of stamina over 6f on good-to-firm, and the prominent group uses itself up tracking her, leaving the hold-up horses with a wall to hit through — though Dash Of Azure and Catching The Moon have the ability and running style to come through late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Holds On, Pace Matches
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is controlled enough that the prominent horses conserve energy and the closers get no meaningful acceleration late.
scenarios.body: With Miss Nightcap dictating a steadier tempo than expected, Royal Fixation or America Queen sit comfortably just behind and produce enough momentum to hold on, rewarding their class and good-to-firm form at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Finds Rail, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-heavy horses mapped to midfield manages to break smartly and claim a forward berth after all.
scenarios.body: Sing The Blues has the most compelling form of the redistributed trio — three wins over this C&D-relevant trip on good ground — and if she secures a prominent position through a good break, her natural front-running ability makes her dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Hold-Up Flounders
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group scrimmages for position and the race breaks into uneven sectionals, denying closers a clear run.
scenarios.body: A bunched early phase followed by a sprint finish can leave hold-up horses with nowhere to go in an 11-runner field on a straight 6f, compressing the race into one flat-out dash that suits whoever is handiest.

watchPoints.text: Watch Miss Nightcap's early lead margin — if she goes uncontested by the 2f pole with a clear gap, she is dangerous to get caught, even in this grade.
Royal Fixation is the class horse on OR 108 and has the best sim-going record in the field; if she travels smoothly in the prominent group, she could prove too strong for the closers.

Sing The Blues broke from a compromised position last time having been shuffled back in a similar shape — watch for Cieren Fallon using the stalls to try to reclaim a forward berth before rivals can react.

Dash Of Azure's last run was at 7f and this is a step down to 6f on a track where pace is set from the front; if the fractions are slower than expected, her hold-up style may not generate enough late momentum.

With three horses (Sing The Blues, Killavia, Ruby's Angel) all effectively racing out of role and mapped to midfield, the 5f-6f section of this race may be unusually congested in the centre of the pack — watch for scrimmaging that could hamper any of the closers Dash Of Azure or Catching The Moon.

races.name: Sky Bet Price Boosts Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: High Degree
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner for William Haggas and Cieren Fallon, with strong form over 10f on good ground (2W6P in similar conditions) but must share the lead with Shoof Baeed this time, which may drain more than it would against softer pace opposition; headgear (p) suggests he needs to be on the bridle early.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and unexposed at the top of these weights, High Degree brings solid recent form — second last time out and third three starts back — to this test, and with experience over today's trip and going, he rates the one to beat despite being yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Ammes
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes the ride on this hold-up performer who has form over 10-12f on good ground and brings a wide range of experience, though the nine-runner recent effort on similar going raises questions; gets into a race where the honest gallop should suit a late runner in theory, but the crowded hold-up division means getting a clean run will be the challenge.

runners_data.name: Jez Bomb
runners_data.note: Shane Gray partners a horse in fine form — three wins in last six — with two recent victories over course-relevant good ground trips; tracks pace naturally and is comfortable at 10f on good, and this race shape of contested leaders plays directly to his ability to deliver a well-timed forward run from a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and with a speed rating that leaves plenty to find against the top-rated runner, Jez Bomb faces a stiff ask here, though he arrives in decent nick — a winner last time out and twice successful in his last six starts — and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Without Compromise
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's hold-up type has a lone win on good ground from five relevant runs (sim-going 0W1P) and has been running on the all-weather primarily; at 1m2f in a field with several closers, getting a clear passage at the right moment will be crucial, and the raw numbers on turf good are modest.
runners_data.comment: Without Compromise showed a return to form with a second last time out after a poor eighth two starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and going in his favour; the 131 lb burden and a mid-ranking profile among these eight may cap his chances.

runners_data.name: Farasi Lane
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's eight-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer — his one win in this sample came from off the pace — but with three hold-up types crowded into the same rear section, he is expected to race closer to midfield than suits him naturally; the style-fit concern (0.93) tempers confidence even if the pace does collapse late.
runners_data.comment: Farasi Lane shaped with promise when third last time out, and a winner three starts back, so he arrives in good heart off a 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going. Carrying 129 lb from stall 6 is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Shoof Baeed
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's lightly-raced three-year-old has only two runs on record, winning over 10f on good last time, and brings the freshness of a 38-day break; a confirmed front-runner who will contest every yard of the lead with High Degree, making him a key pace-shape setter rather than the most likely winner if that duel turns costly.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back but only sixth last time out, and our rating of 72 — well below his official mark — places him last of eight in this field; has run over today's trip and going, and stall two is at least a neutral draw.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's runner is a genuine closer — he prefers to come from off the pace — but is mapped to midfield because the rear section is oversubscribed; the style-fit flag (0.92) reflects the mismatch, and while his good-ground form is the strongest in the field (13/15 runs on similar going), racing outside his comfort zone in a prominent slot blunts his chance.
runners_data.comment: Financer won three starts back but was seventh last time out, leaving him with something to prove here; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 127 lb from stall eight, and our rating of 82 suggests a shade more than his official mark credits.

runners_data.name: Mr Seagull
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old has modest form (0 recent wins, light experience) and is a natural hold-up type who, like Farasi Lane and Financer, will find himself forward of his ideal position as the rear of the field is congested; the variable (v) ground tag and limited sim-going record (1W1P from 9) add further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and coming off an unplaced effort 17 days ago, Mr Seagull nonetheless rates considerably higher than his official mark of 74 suggests, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main risk is a trainer in desperate form at just 1 from 29 over the past fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: High Degree and Shoof Baeed are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 1m2f trip at Pontefract, creating a genuinely contested gallop on Good to Firm ground rather than an artificial tempo set by a lone pace-setter. Jez Bomb, racing prominently, will sit just off the duelling leaders and adds further pressure to the early sections, meaning the pace will be honest and sustained throughout. This contested dynamic stretches the field, burns out the leaders through the home straight, and sets the race up for horses with tactical speed who can travel close to the pace without being consumed by it — a prominent-to-midfield profile that can pick up smoothly once the front two cry enough is best placed here. The field carries more genuine hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Farasi Lane, Financer, and Mr Seagull are true closers who will find themselves further forward than ideal and unlikely to secure their natural position in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If High Degree and Shoof Baeed fight for the lead and burn each other out, leaving the prominent tracker to inherit the prize
scenarios.body: The two leaders set a demanding gallop that drains their reserves in the final two furlongs, handing the race to the horse that has sat just behind the pressure and timed their run to perfection; Jez Bomb, with two recent wins and a profile built on tracking pace on good ground, is ideally positioned to pounce from this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Shoof Baeed or High Degree settles into a rhythm, controls the fractions, and keeps enough in reserve to hold on
scenarios.body: One of the front pair manages to assert crossing the halfway point and gradually winds up the tempo without breaking their own momentum, leaving pursuers unable to close the gap late; the Good to Firm ground rewards a horse with a high cruising speed and the fitness to sustain it over 1m2f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Raider Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace is genuinely fierce enough to open the door for a horse tracking in midfield who has been sheltered from the battle
scenarios.body: Without Compromise or Ammes, sitting off the early tempo with cover, could find the gaps opening in the final furlong as the front pair weaken together; this shape is less straightforward to execute given the number of horses who want similar ground in the middle of the race, but the honest gallop does create a theoretical runway for a well-timed run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Denied By Pace Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow steadies mid-race after the early duel, compressing the field and leaving closers blocked behind traffic
scenarios.body: Financer, Farasi Lane, and Mr Seagull are all true hold-up horses racing out of their natural role and would need near-perfect circumstances to thread through; this scenario is heavily discounted because the shape that would benefit them is precisely the one least likely to materialise given the confirmed front-running duel at the head of affairs.

watchPoints.text: Watch the duel between High Degree and Shoof Baeed in the first three furlongs — if they go toe-to-toe at a true gallop, both are at significant risk of tying up in the straight and handing the race to Jez Bomb.

Jez Bomb's draw and early positioning will be critical — if he is denied his natural prominent slot by the front-running duel drifting wide, his ability to dominate from behind the pace is compromised.

Ammes, Without Compromise, Farasi Lane, Financer, and Mr Seagull all want rear or midfield berths in the same race; watch for traffic congestion in the straight as several of these converge simultaneously with limited room to manoeuvre.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this 1m2f slot — faster than the declared GOOD, which will amplify the cost of the early contested pace and reward horses with sound action and class rather than those relying on stamina grinding rivals down.

Shoof Baeed's inexperience (only two career runs) is worth monitoring in running — if he shows greenness or fails to settle in front under pressure from High Degree, his chance dissolves quickly and the complexion of the whole race changes.

races.name: Sky Bet Build A Bet Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Badri
runners_data.note: Supremely course-and-distance fit (four wins at 5-6f on Good) and in sharp form with a win six days ago; prominent style suits the projected race shape ideally, and Jason Hart's handling of forward-going sprinters is a notable positive at 9yo.
runners_data.comment: Badri has won four times in his last six starts, including back-to-back wins two and three starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is that unplaced effort last time out at just six days' rest leaves his current form slightly in the air.

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Won on Good over 5f on her most recent start and has a solid prominent style that matches the likely race shape; trainer Bethell in fine form (8/24 over 14 days) and Oisin Orr retaining the ride is a positive continuity angle.
runners_data.comment: Fluorescence arrives here on the back of a placing last time out and has run over today's trip and going, with a yard firing at 33% in the past fortnight providing strong support; the risk is that she remains winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Baker Blue
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner and will set the tempo from stall to post; his form figures on Good going over 5f are patchy (0 wins from 4 runs in similar conditions) which is a mild concern, but Callum Rodriguez is adept at front-running rides and he gets a clear lead.
runners_data.comment: Baker Blue showed well when a second two starts back, but comes into this off a sixth last time out; he has run over today's trip and going before, and at 133 lb from stall six, faces a stiff ask to reverse recent form.

runners_data.name: Rocking Ends
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on Good in recent form and has an outstanding 5f profile at Pontefract (13 runs, 4 wins, 5 places); the visor is worn again and Cieren Fallon is a high-quality booking — prominent style is perfectly suited to the expected race shape.
runners_data.comment: Rocking Ends won two starts back and returns in good order after 22 days, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; a fifth last time out tempers enthusiasm slightly, but he carries 132 lb from stall four and looks a solid each-way proposition.

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Out-and-out hold-up horse who has struggled in similar company lately (six, eight, twelve, fifteen in last four); visored again and Paul Mulrennan is the right pilot, but a sustainable pace on fast ground is not what this horse needs and his Good-going record at 5f reads poorly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and only lightly threatening in that recent sequence, Kylian does bring distance and going experience to the table, and 22 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the 131 lb burden, however, makes improvement a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Vintage Clarets
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has placed at 5f on soft but his Good-ground form over 5f shows consistent mid-to-low finishes; the 5lb claimer Ethan Tindall takes valuable weight off, but getting competitive from the rear on a quick-draining Pontefract 5f is genuinely difficult.
runners_data.comment: Vintage Clarets shaped with real promise when third two starts back and second three starts back, and he arrives here fit on 19 days' rest with experience of today's distance and going; the concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Won twice at 5f on Good ground recently which is strong form, but this is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping because there are too many closers for the rear of the field — his true style means he will be further back than the map shows, which reduces his chance in a shape dominated by front and prominent runners.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins two and three starts back gave One And Gone brief momentum, but he was unplaced last time out and our figures rank him seventh of eight, making him hard to fancy despite having experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Reigning Profit
runners_data.note: Has a 5f Pontefract win on Good in recent form and is bred to handle these conditions; a natural prominent racer in reality, but with Badri, Fluorescence and Rocking Ends all ahead of him in the queue for those early positions, he may not secure the pitch he needs — his chance is tempered by that overcrowding.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and unplaced last time out, Reigning Profit makes a difficult proposition, though he does bring a win three starts back and experience of today's distance and going, carrying 121 lb from stall seven on a 19-day turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Baker Blue is the lone confirmed front-runner and on Good to Firm ground over 5f at Pontefract will look to dictate from the off, setting a brisk but controlled tempo that need not be suicidal given the absence of a genuine challenger for the lead. Badri, Fluorescence and Rocking Ends are all prominent types who will press forward and contest the early positions behind Baker Blue, creating a compressed front group rather than a truly lone leader scenario. The field actually contains more pace than the positional map can accommodate — Reigning Profit is a natural prominent racer who will struggle to secure that berth, and One And Gone is a genuine hold-up type who has been pushed into a midfield mapping because the rear is oversubscribed; neither is racing in their most comfortable role. A controlled-but-honest pace on fast ground over a sharp 5f shapes this race to favour horses who can race prominently in the first three or four and sustain their effort to the line — hold-up horses face a stiff ask getting competitive from off the pace on a track where the straight is short and ground is fast.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Baker Blue leads at a sustainable gallop and the prominent horses Badri, Rocking Ends and Fluorescence race in his slipstream, the race becomes a stamina-and-speed test for the front four.
scenarios.body: Baker Blue sets fractions comfortable enough to preserve his finishing kick, while the pressing prominent horses have enough position to pounce inside the final furlong without needing to find an impossible gear from the rear; Good to Firm ground rewards those who travel prominently and sustain rather than sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Baker Blue goes off too fast under pressure from the prominent group and the pace genuinely collapses in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A frenetic early pace burns out the front-runners in the final 100 yards, and any horse who has been able to switch off and coast through midfield gets a rare opportunity to swoop; Vintage Clarets and Kylian, genuine hold-up types, would be the primary beneficiaries of a true pace collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Overcrowding Causes Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types — Badri, Rocking Ends and Fluorescence — all push hard to sit second and third, creating a scrappy mid-race scramble for position.
scenarios.body: Interference and energy expended fighting for berths in the first half of the race could leave several prominent horses flat when the run begins; a horse like Rocking Ends who is robust and experienced in tight company could benefit from the chaos while others are checked.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Confusion
scenarios.trigger: If the pace scenario is chaotic enough that no single horse controls the tempo and the race fragments into multiple small groups.
scenarios.body: Reigning Profit, despite being mapped out of a natural prominent role, has the 5f course fitness and Good to Firm record to capitalise if gifted a clean passage; One And Gone's two wins at this trip on this ground are relevant if the pace unexpectedly softens and hold-up horses get a meaningful target to aim at.

watchPoints.text: Baker Blue's unbeaten record in similar going (0 wins from 4 on Good at 5f) is a red flag — if he ties up inside the final furlong after leading, the prominent group directly behind him will swamp him and the result hinges entirely on what follows.

Rocking Ends has the strongest course-and-distance profile in the race (4 wins from 13 at Pontefract 5f) and arrives in form — if Cieren Fallon slots him into second or third early, he is the primary threat to any leader who does not sustain.

The cluster of Badri, Fluorescence and Rocking Ends all wanting the same prominent positions creates a genuine early-race flashpoint — watch the first furlong for bumping or checking as they sort out the order.

One And Gone's two recent 5f Good-ground wins look eye-catching but his natural style means he will trail the field early; if he is seen making headway turning for home, the pace has genuinely collapsed and the hold-up scenario is live.

Good to Firm ground confirmed for this race — any horse with a going concern on quick ground should be monitored in pre-race; the faster the ground, the more it rewards prominent gallopers over late finishers at Pontefract's short home straight.

races.name: Sky Bet Extra Places Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer whose recent form of 5th in a handicap over 16f on Good suggests he stays well and handles this ground; Charlie Johnston yard in fair nick at T14:4/33, Jason Hart takes the ride, and 8 days since last run is a positive freshness angle over this trip.
runners_data.comment: Pole Star rates 12 lb above his official mark on our figures and, ranked second of the six runners, shapes as a leading player; he has run over today's trip and going before and returns fit on just eight days' rest, though his recent sequence shows him winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Laafy
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran whose visor headgear is retained, returning after 50 days off for Brian Ellison; has posted five consecutive placed or out-of-frame finishes and his similar-going record of 7/15 is less impressive than rivals, making this a tough ask despite his prominent racing style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Laafy nonetheless rates narrowly top of our figures and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the 50-day break is worth noting, but at 141 lb he remains the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Letsbefrank
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has won three of his last five and arrives 57 days fresh for Jim Goldie; similar-going figures of 10/15 are only moderate but his last two course-type efforts over shorter ground show real improvement — the step back up to 17f may actually suit this stayer.
runners_data.comment: Letsbefrank showed his best when winning back-to-back two and three starts back, and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a strong each-way claims; the main risk is a return from 57 days off after a below-par sixth last time out.

runners_data.name: Sixty Plus
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins, all front-running, all on Good, and a career-best recent profile makes this horse the most in-form runner in the field; Cieren Fallon takes the ride and the visor is retained, though the step up to 17f from 14f and the prospect of a contested lead from Treasure Islands are the primary risks to his winning streak.
runners_data.comment: Sixty Plus has winning form — three victories in his last six starts — but our rating places him fifth of six here, and that speed figure of 69 gives little encouragement against this field; the going experience is a mild plus, and he arrives fresh enough on 17 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: David Allan rides this front-runner who won over 16f earlier in the season but whose last four runs have produced two wins and two poor efforts; the similar-going record of 6/11 is workable, though contesting the lead with Sixty Plus over this trip risks burning both horses out before the home straight.
runners_data.comment: Treasure Islands won four starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, giving him a solid platform off 128 lb, and his speed rating of 82 underlines he holds strong claims here; the worry is that three subsequent outings have yielded only a sixth and seventh.

runners_data.name: Campeona
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old has won three of her last four and carries a pacemaker headgear flag; lightly weighted at 120lbs and hold-up in style, she arrives on 15 days' rest with the best recent momentum in the field, though her similar-going stats of just 2/7 on fast ground and the jump in trip to 17f from 16f represent the key unknowns to assess.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures despite an official mark of 73, Campeona faces a stiff ask, yet her recent form is eye-catching — a winner three times in her last five starts, with a run just 15 days ago suggesting she arrives in good heart, and she has experience of today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Sixty Plus and Treasure Islands are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead over 2m1f on good-to-firm ground at Pontefract, creating an honest, pressured gallop from the outset rather than a falsely-run crawl. Sixty Plus arrives in career-best form with three consecutive wins, all at 14f or shorter, and will be keen to dictate; Treasure Islands has also won over 16f and will push for the rail, meaning neither is likely to yield without a fight. Pole Star and Laafy will track from a prominent position, while Letsbefrank and Campeona are both hold-up types who will settle at the rear and rely on picking up late. With a genuine pace duel setting the tempo for a staying trip on fast ground, this race shape is classically biased towards horses who can settle off the pace and finish through the field — hold-up and late-running profiles are favoured, provided the strong early fractions don't burn out the leaders entirely before the home turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Burns Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Sixty Plus and Treasure Islands fight for supremacy and sustain a strong gallop throughout the 2m1f trip, the early pressure causes both to weaken in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The contested lead drains both front-runners in the final two furlongs, leaving the race wide open for closers to sweep through from the rear; over this stamina-sapping trip on good-to-firm ground, hold-up horses who conserve energy early are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Sixty Plus successfully shakes off Treasure Islands early and is allowed to control a sustainable gallop unchallenged from the front.
scenarios.body: With a comfortable lead and no serious pressure to contend with, Sixty Plus can settle into a rhythm that exploits his current outstanding form of three consecutive wins; prominent types who track him closely without burning fuel would be next best.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel is competitive but not truly brutal, leaving the prominent pair of Pole Star and Laafy close enough to the action to capitalise.
scenarios.body: A moderate pace contest allows horses tracking the leaders to sit within striking range and pounce before the hold-up horses can generate momentum; Pole Star's course form and Laafy's consistent prominent-running style both suit a race decided in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail to Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly steady and the front-runners conserve enough energy to hold off the hold-up horses despite the long trip.
scenarios.body: A moderate early gallop over 2m1f could allow the leaders to control tempo and resist the late challenge from Campeona and Letsbefrank, who need strong fractions to generate their finishing kicks.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sixty Plus or Treasure Islands blinks first in the early furlongs — if neither concedes the lead, the sustained duel over 2m1f on good-to-firm ground could fatally compromise both horses before they turn for home.

Campeona's headgear flag and hold-up style suggest Prescott has trained her specifically for this trip, but her limited similar-going record of 2/7 on fast ground must be monitored if the ground rides quicker than reported.

Letsbefrank arrives 57 days since last run for Jim Goldie, whose T14 figure of 3/43 is a notably poor strike rate — watch for any signs of rustiness in the paddock or early in the race before trusting the in-form profile.

Laafy's 50-day absence combined with a career record that shows no win on good-to-firm ground in recent outings makes the veteran one to watch for early signs of whether the return suits before committing to his chance.

The final-furlong terrain at Pontefract is famously uphill and sharp, favouring horses who have been produced with a strong run rather than those who have led from tape to tape — worth tracking where Campeona and Letsbefrank sit at the two-furlong pole.

races.name: Sky Bet Proud To Support Young Lives Vs Cancer Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: Boasts a course-and-distance win on good ground and sets the pace here by default, but the STYLE_FIT flag suggests she is not truly in her optimal role, and her recent form includes several placed efforts without winning — her control of the race may flatter her finishing position.

runners_data.name: Alfa Whiteburd
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins heading into this, all on good ground over 6-7f, make her a major player — Jason Hart is an excellent partner, and while she is a natural hold-up horse she has the class and recent momentum to overcome a less-than-perfect tactical scenario.
runners_data.comment: Alfa Whiteburd arrives in cracking nick with three wins in his last six starts, including back-to-back victories, and only 11 days between runs keeps him fresh; he has run over today's trip and going before, though carrying 136 lb from stall six may test his resolve.

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has a winning run on soft ground over 7f in recent starts — the step back to 6f on faster ground is a query, and her true hold-up style means she needs rivals to tire in front of her; 37 days off is not a concern given trainer Richard Hughes keeps horses fresh.
runners_data.comment: Rare Change won two starts back but has shown inconsistency either side of that success, finishing seventh last time out and ninth three starts back; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 37 days off leaves fitness a minor question, though a rating of 86 keeps him competitive from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Russet Gold
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has drawn a blank in nine recent starts on good ground, failing to place in any of them — a genuine hold-up type who is mapped to midfield but will likely race even further back, and without a pace collapse there is little evidence to suggest he can reverse that trend here.
runners_data.comment: Russet Gold is winless in his last five starts, yet our rating of 99 ranks him ahead of all nine runners here, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the trainer's current 3% strike rate over the past fortnight is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has run consistently without quite winning, placing twice recently over this C&D in good ground — her hold-up style is genuine but she has the finishing speed to threaten if the pace sets up for closers, and David O'Meara's yard is in good form with nine wins from 51 runners over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Yes I'm Mali has been knocking on the door, finishing second on three occasions in recent starts, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset at 133 lb from stall two; the risk is that he has yet to convert, and that seventh last time out raises a question mark.

runners_data.name: The Good Biscuit
runners_data.note: Two wins in recent starts for Joanna Mason, both over this exact C&D trip in good ground — her prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking Veblen Good in a race with limited front-running competition, and 11 days between runs is no issue given her current form.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins before his latest sixth give The Good Biscuit a strong recent profile, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; drawn four and carrying 132 lb, the key question is whether that weight blunts his momentum on the back of a below-par run.

runners_data.name: Havana Rum
runners_data.note: In reality a hold-up horse who will race behind midfield despite the map position; best efforts on good ground over 6f include two thirds recently, but the redistribution context means he is unlikely to get the strongly-run race he needs to fire from the back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with two thirds in that spell the best he can offer, Havana Rum faces a stiff ask ranked seventh of nine on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and an eighth last time out at least leaves room for a bounce-back.

runners_data.name: Mondammej
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old whose recent form is over 5f — stepping up to 6f at Pontefract is a different test, and while he is placed here in midfield, his natural instinct is to race from the rear; the distance question and advancing age make this a tall ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Mondammej is hard to fancy despite a return to familiar distance and going and a run just 15 days ago keeping him fit.

runners_data.name: Fiscal Policy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has recorded a win and two places on good ground over 6f in his last five starts — though naturally a hold-up runner placed in midfield on the map, his consistent placed form over C&D suggests he is not without a chance if the closers do get a run through.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and winless in his last five starts, Fiscal Policy faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround that at least suggests he is fit.

races.paceDynamic: Veblen Good is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Pontefract, and with no obvious challenger for the lead, she can bowl along at a controlled, uncontested tempo that suits a horse who has already won over this trip and course combination. The Good Biscuit is the only other prominently-styled runner and will likely slot in just behind, creating a small leading group with the remainder tracking in behind. This sustainable, single-pace shape with no early battle for supremacy suits hold-up horses who can close from a position behind a steady gallop — though with Russet Gold, Havana Rum, Mondammej and Fiscal Policy all being true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map, the rear of this field is genuinely congested with horses unlikely to get their natural position. The race shape, with one horse controlling matters from the front at a measured clip on fast ground, most favours a prominent or close-tracking runner who can make a smooth move from the home turn without being trapped in traffic — benefiting The Good Biscuit and Alfa Whiteburd, who can track up and pounce, over horses who need a strongly-run race to land their winning blow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Veblen Controls, Tracked Home
scenarios.trigger: If Veblen Good leads uncontested and The Good Biscuit tracks into a winning position rounding the home turn.
scenarios.body: Veblen Good dictates a steady, sustainable gallop with The Good Biscuit sitting close enough to strike in the straight, and on good-to-firm ground the advantage stays with those who hold a prominent tracking position from the outset. Hold-up horses are left with too little ground to close as the pace is not strong enough to open a gap for them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Overcome Steady Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that hold-up horses with genuine turn-of-foot can weave through to win despite the modest gallop.
scenarios.body: Alfa Whiteburd, in blistering in-form shape with three recent wins, has the class and finishing speed to make ground even if the pace is only fair, and Yes I'm Mali has repeatedly found the line in this sort of race from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Two Fade
scenarios.trigger: If a mid-race injection of pace causes Veblen Good and The Good Biscuit to overextend and tie up in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A sharper early tempo would leave the front two vulnerable late, allowing closers with stamina to pick them off — Rare Change's recent 7f form and Havana Rum's best efforts on similar ground suggest they could profit from any breakdown of the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds Every Challenge
scenarios.trigger: If Veblen Good establishes a decisive lead and her rivals mistime their challenges, allowing her to win comfortably despite her STYLE_FIT flag.
scenarios.body: Though operating slightly out of role, Veblen Good's strong course and distance record on good ground makes her capable of converting if rivals leave their challenges too late. The Good Biscuit would be the likely runner-up if the hold-up horses are simply unable to bridge the gap.

watchPoints.text: Alfa Whiteburd enters on the back of three wins and holds a clear class edge on recent form — if Jason Hart can get her into a prominent position early rather than having to close from the back of the pack, she becomes the most dangerous horse in the race.

The Good Biscuit and Veblen Good are the only two horses naturally suited to racing up with the pace — watch how quickly The Good Biscuit moves to sit behind the leader in the early stages, as her position at the 3f mark will largely determine her winning chance.

With Russet Gold, Havana Rum, Mondammej and Fiscal Policy all true hold-up horses forced to race in midfield, there is a risk of traffic and crowding on the home turn — horses drawn on the outside may get a cleaner passage than those trapped on the inner.

Pontefract's 6f course has a long straight after a sharp left-hand bend — horses who make their move too early on the turn can flatten out, meaning runners who wait until they are fully in the straight before challenging tend to sustain their effort better on fast ground.

The going is confirmed good-to-firm for this race, which suits horses with clean recent form on similar ground — Yes I'm Mali and The Good Biscuit both have strong records in these conditions and their fitness credentials are current given both ran 11-22 days ago.
